theorem erdos_1094__h2__h2__h3__h1 : ∃ (K : ℕ),
  ∀ (n k : ℕ),
    (0 : ℕ) < k →
      k * k * k ≤ n →
        Real.exp (Real.log (↑k : ℝ) ^ (2 : ℕ) / ((20 : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (↑k : ℝ)))) < (↑n : ℝ) + (1 : ℝ) →
          k * (n / k) ∣ k.factorial → (n.choose k).minFac > n / k → Nat.Prime (n / n.gcd k) → k ≤ K := by
  sorry

references.note: Conjectures that for n > k^2 the binomial coefficient C(n,k) has a prime factor p <= n/k. This node is the finitely-many form of that conjecture on a sub-range. Cited through erdosproblems.com/384, read 2026-11-11.
references.title: E. F. Ecklund, Jr., On prime divisors of the binomial coefficient, Pacific J. Math. 29 (1969) 267-270

references.note: Listed open; page read 2026-11-11 (last edited 24 October 2025). No proof claim is recorded there.
references.title: Erdős problem #1094 (erdosproblems.com), with Selfridge's conjecture (n >= k^2 - 1, single exception C(62,6))

references.note: Section 2 (pp. 521-523): the conjecture lpf C(N,k) <= max(N/k, k) with 14 exceptions, Selfridge's conjecture for N >= k^2 - 1, the deficiency, and the remark that an exception needs b_j = 1 at the multiple of k. No theorem on this range. Read 2026-11-11.
references.title: P. Erdős, C. B. Lacampagne and J. L. Selfridge, Prime factors of binomial coefficients and related problems, Acta Arith. 49 (1988) 507-523

references.note: An exception with n >= k^2 has n >= g(k). Records k^(1+c) < g(k) <= exp((1+o(1))k) (Ecklund-Erdős-Selfridge 1974) and g(k) >= exp(c (log k)^2) (Konyagin 1999) as the best bounds. Read 2026-11-11.
references.title: Erdős problem #1095 (erdosproblems.com): g(k), the least n > k+1 with every prime factor of C(n,k) above k

references.note: g(k) >= exp(c log^2 k). Abstract and reference list read on the journal's page 2026-11-11; the paper itself not read (paywall).
references.title: S. V. Konyagin, Estimates of the least prime factor of a binomial coefficient, Mathematika 46 (1999) 41-55

references.note: Theorem 1.1 removes every n <= exp(log^2 k/(20 log log k)); this node is what lies beyond it. Paper read 2026-11-11. Its last range is the edge of the method, not of the problem.
references.title: W. van Doorn and Q. Tang, Consecutive integers free of certain prime factors, arXiv:2606.19863 (2026)

references.note: Heuristic model: log g(k) is of order k/log k (constant 0.788 in the addendum). So conjecturally this node's range holds no candidate below about exp(0.79 k/log k). Addendum read 2026-11-11.
references.title: B. Sorenson, J. Sorenson and J. Webster, An algorithm and estimates for the Erdős-Selfridge function, ANTS XIV, Open Book Series 4 (2020) 371-385; addendum arXiv:1907.08559v3

literature_proposed.summary: Open. The statement is Ecklund's conjecture in finitely-many form (Selfridge conjectured the sharper form with the single exception C(62,6)), restricted to n >= k^3 and n beyond van Doorn and Tang's range exp(log^2 k/(20 log log k)). Nothing is known for n between exp(c log^2 k) and k 2^(k-1): below g(k) the statement is implied by lower bounds for g(k) (Erdős problem 1095), where Konyagin's exp(c log^2 k) of 1999 is the record, and from g(k) upwards no method is known that forces a prime of (k, n/k] to divide one of k given consecutive integers. Above k 2^(k-1) + k there is no exception (annex on this node, elementary). I found no paper or forum claim of a proof or of a partial result on this range; Erdős-Lacampagne-Selfridge (1988), read today, state it as a conjecture, and erdosproblems.com/1094 and /384 list it open. Their 1993 paper I could not open.
